def min_assembly_cost(base, interference, prereq):
    """Compute the minimum total cost of installing all n components of a
    gadget, one at a time, in some order of your choice.

    There are n components, numbered 0..n-1, where n = len(base) and
    1 <= n <= 12.

    Installing component i as the k-th installation (k = 1, 2, ..., n)
    costs:

        base[i] * k  +  sum of interference[j][i] over every component j
                        that was already installed before i

    The total cost of an order is the sum of these installation costs.

    Input domain:
      - base: list of n ints, 0 <= base[i] <= 100.
      - interference: n x n list of lists of ints,
        0 <= interference[j][i] <= 100 and interference[i][i] == 0.
        interference[j][i] is the surcharge paid when i is installed
        while j is already in place (it need not equal interference[i][j]).
      - prereq: list of n lists; prereq[i] contains distinct component
        indices (never i itself) that must all be installed strictly
        before component i may be installed. Prerequisites may chain
        and may be contradictory (cyclic).

    Return the minimum achievable total cost over all installation orders
    that satisfy every prerequisite, as an int. If no order satisfies the
    prerequisites, return -1.

    Examples:

    >>> min_assembly_cost([1, 10], [[0, 5], [0, 0]], [[], []])
    12
    >>> min_assembly_cost([1, 10], [[0, 5], [0, 0]], [[], [0]])
    26
    >>> min_assembly_cost([2, 3, 1], [[0, 4, 0], [1, 0, 6], [0, 2, 0]],
    ...                   [[], [], [0]])
    17
    >>> min_assembly_cost([1, 1], [[0, 0], [0, 0]], [[1], [0]])
    -1
    """
